title: Hardy-Weinberg heterozygote frequency for MN blood group alleles
learningObjectives: Predict heterozygote frequency 2pq from allele frequency p in a large randomly mating population.
Explain that allele frequencies p and q = 1 - p determine expected genotype frequencies p², 2pq and q².
Interpret why heterozygote frequency is maximized at p = 0.5 and falls to zero when p approaches fixation.

explanations.text: The Hardy-Weinberg principle predicts that allele frequencies remain constant across generations when a population is large and randomly mating and no evolutionary forces act, providing a baseline to detect change.

evidence.quote: The Hardy-Weinberg principle states that in a large randomly breeding population, allelic frequencies will remain the same
In order for a population to be considered to be in equilibrium, it must remain the same from generation to generation.

explanations.text: For a two-allele system frequencies are p for the first allele and q = 1 - p for the second, giving expected genotype frequencies p², 2pq and q² in the next generation.
